Run cost data report

Summary

  • Antigravity generation finished with 29 SUCCESS runs, 1 ERROR, and 7 empty replies; every other assistant-stage combination recorded only SUCCESS runs and no empty replies.
  • Qwen had the largest reported generation cost, totaling 50.98 hours and 709.11 million tokens processed across 30 runs; its reviews totaled 34.53 hours and 402.96 million tokens across 48 runs.
  • Codex processed 8.28 million tokens in generation and 65.42 million in review, but it did not report run time.
  • In the recovered pilot, Claude Sonnet 5 at max effort used 30.24 minutes and 1.24 million tokens processed, versus 4.38 minutes and 0.24 million for Claude Opus 5 at medium on the same task.
  • Qwen’s Security-informed setting paired xhigh generation with medium review: generation took 358.46 minutes per program and self-review took 46.38 minutes, with a review / generation value of 0.13.

Reader’s rule: time and tokens describe the coding assistant as configured (model, effort setting, scaffolding and hardware), not the model alone. Codex records no run time, so it is absent from every time figure.

What was measured

Source of the numbers

This report separates generation runs, attributed to the assistant that wrote each program, from review runs, attributed to the assistant that reviewed it. The tables and figures summarize completion status and the time, tokens, and turns reported by each assistant’s CLI.

  • A generation run is one assistant writing one program. Its cost belongs to the generator.
  • A review run is one reviewer reading one program. Its cost belongs to the reviewer.

Two token measures, one rule for every assistant

The token-accounting table distinguishes each assistant’s reported input, cache, and output fields. Throughout the report, tokens processed includes the components shown in the final column, while generated tokens refers to output.

How each assistant reports tokens, and the measure this report derives from them
Assistant What “input” counts Cached tokens Tool’s own total Tokens processed, as used here
Antigravity input not read from cache reported separately input + output input + cached read + output
Claude Code input not read from or written to cache reported separately, plus cache creation input + output input + cache creation + cached read + output
Codex all input, cached included already inside input input + output input + output
Qwen Code the whole prompt, re-sent on every request not reported input + output input + output

Gaps in the data

Codex did not report run time, so its time values are missing from Table 3 and it is omitted from the time figures. Table 1 and Table 2 also identify generation runs that ended in ERROR or returned an empty reply.

How the runs finished

In Table 1, Antigravity generation recorded 29 SUCCESS runs, 1 ERROR, and 7 empty replies among 30 runs. Each of the other generation rows recorded 30 SUCCESS runs, while all four review rows recorded 48 SUCCESS runs; none of those rows had an ERROR or empty reply.

All 7 runs in Table 2 were Antigravity generation runs with empty replies: 1 ended in ERROR and 6 ended in SUCCESS. Their reported times ranged from 4.8 to 5.0 minutes.

Overall cost per assistant

Table 3 shows Qwen with the largest totals for both stages: generation used 50.98 hours and 709.11 million tokens processed, while review used 34.53 hours and 402.96 million tokens. Codex reported 8.28 million generation tokens and 65.42 million review tokens, but its total hours and mean minutes per run were not reported.

Generation

Figure 1 shows Qwen taking longer to generate programs than Antigravity or Claude in every condition, with the separation especially pronounced for Security-informed programs. For all three timed generators, Security-informed generation is longer than Basic and Security-aware generation.

Figure 2 shows Qwen processing the most tokens per generated program in every condition, followed by Antigravity, while Claude and Codex are lower. Every generator’s Security-informed bar is its highest of the three conditions.

Across the task-level time panels in Figure 3, Qwen is the slowest timed generator for every task and condition. Its Security-informed times are much higher than its Basic and Security-aware times, while Antigravity and Claude vary within a narrower range.

Figure 4 shows Qwen processing the most tokens for every task-condition combination. Security-informed tasks generally occupy the highest-token panel for each generator, with the strongest contrast visible for Qwen.

Review

Figure 5 shows Qwen self-reviews taking longer than Antigravity and Claude self-reviews in all three conditions. Security-informed self-review is the longest condition for Antigravity and Claude, whereas Qwen’s self-review time decreases from Basic through Security-informed.

In Figure 6, Qwen processes the most tokens per self-review in every condition, followed by Antigravity, Codex, and Claude. Security-informed self-review is the highest-token condition for Antigravity, Claude, and Codex, while Qwen peaks under Security-aware.

Figure 7 shows Qwen as the highest-token reviewer across all generator columns for both tokens processed and tokens generated. Reviews of Qwen-generated programs are generally among the largest within each reviewer row, while reviews of Codex-generated programs are generally the smallest.

Claude at maximum effort in the pilot

This section compares the recovered Claude Sonnet 5 pilot at max effort with Claude Opus 5 at medium for Task 1 Basic generation. The table covers reported minutes, output and thinking tokens, thinking share, tokens processed, and turns, and also gives the Opus mean across its 12 Basic runs.

In Table 4, the Sonnet 5 max pilot used 30.24 minutes, 166076.0 output tokens, 139895.0 thinking tokens, 1.24 million tokens processed, and 21.0 turns. On the same task, Opus 5 medium used 4.38 minutes, 23639.0 output tokens, 7475.0 thinking tokens, 0.24 million tokens processed, and 12.0 turns; the reported Sonnet / Opus values were 6.91, 7.03, 18.72, 5.12, and 1.75 for those measures, respectively.

Qwen review effort

This section compares Qwen generation and self-review time across conditions and their associated effort settings. It also presents actual Security-informed review hours at medium and the table’s estimated hours at xhigh for both the self-review subset and the full four-generator panel.

Figure 8 shows self-review taking longer than generation for Basic and Security-aware programs, where both stages used xhigh effort. For Security-informed programs, xhigh generation is much longer than medium-effort self-review.

In Table 5, Basic generation and self-review took 36.11 and 51.75 minutes, with a review / generation value of 1.43; Security-aware took 39.56 and 48.76 minutes, with 1.23. Security-informed used xhigh generation and medium review, taking 358.46 and 46.38 minutes, with 0.13.

Table 6 reports 4.6 actual hours at medium and 47.6 estimated hours at xhigh for 6 self-reviews. For 24 reviews across all four generators, it reports 14.4 actual hours at medium and 190.5 estimated hours at xhigh.

Figure 9 visually shows the xhigh estimates well above the actual medium-effort hours for both Qwen review scopes. The gap is larger for the full panel of reviews than for the self-review subset.

Reading these numbers

The reported time and token measures describe each configured assistant and its runs. Generation cost belongs to the generator and review cost to the reviewer, while Codex time remains unreported; comparisons involving Qwen Security-informed review also reflect its medium review effort rather than xhigh.
